sections.heading: How to Play Discipline
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Discipline"][color=q1]Discipline Priest Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
Healing, in general, has less of a strict rotation and more of a priority list. Discipline tends to follow 3 key rules:

[center][box]
[center][wrapper width=800px]
[table]
[tr]
[td width=7%][icon name=spell_holy_painsupression size=medium type=round color=priest inline=true][/icon][/td] 
[td][b]Always be casting:[/b]  Ensure that you are always maintaining [spell=589] and casting [spell=47540]/[spell=8092] and [spell=585] during downtime to make the most of your [spell=81749] buffs. These smaller heals during downtime really add up over the course of an encounter and with our new set bonus granting Void Shields from Mind Blast you never want to miss a cast or delay it for more than a couple seconds![/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
[tr]
[td width=7%][icon name=spell_holy_penance size=medium type=round color=priest inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b]Discipline is a "Ramping" Healer:[/b] Discipline Priests thrive in a raid environment where they are covering specific and consistent damage events that they can prepare for. Sites like [url=https://lorrgs.io/]Lorrgs[/url] are amazing when preparing for raid encounters so you can observe trends where other players used their cooldowns to burst for the most healing. Knowing what mechanics require "ramping" up your [spell=81749] count to then unleash a flurry of damage abilities is absolutely imperative to your success.[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
[tr][td width=7%][icon name=spell_shadow_summonvoidwalker size=medium type=round color=priest inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b]Mythic+ Healing can be polarizing:[/b] Discipline is at its strongest with cooldowns like [spell=472433] or your Voidweaver Rift. While in a raid group, you can count on other Healers to compensate for periods of lower healing from you while you are in your cooldown period. In dungeons, however, you need to be prepared to compensate for when you are lacking a cooldown all on your own. That means that smart usage of the revamped [spell=197862], which brings a flat heal and absorption increase, or your damage reduction in [spell=33206] is key to mitigating damage on your allies when you are not as easily able to heal them up. [spell=421453] is also a powerful cooldown that also doubles as a large defensive so try to find times to cast this when you and your team are taking heavy damage.[/td][/tr][/table]
[/wrapper][/center]
[/box][/center]
[pad]
[center][cta-button guide=32986 icon=spell_holy_powerwordshield]Discipline Priest Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority

[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=spell_holy_powerwordshield type=round size=medium inline=true color=q1][/icon] Best Discipline Priest Rotation[/h2]

[b]Stop your Camera moving during Penance
[/b]

This input is a one-time console command that you can paste and enter into your chat box and will stop your camera from moving all over the place when you are Penancing an ally. Note that your character will still turn!
[code]/console cameraSmoothTrackingStyle 0[/code]

[b]Key Macros[/b]

These [spell=585] and [spell=47540] macros allow you to spam each spell even when [spell=47540] is channeling and it will not "clip" or interrupt the [spell=47540] channel, allowing you to guarantee that all bolts are launched before you begin your next cast. 
[code]#showtooltip Smite
/cast [@mouseover,harm,nodead,nochanneling:penance,nochanneling:dark reprimand][nochanneling:penance,nochanneling:dark reprimand] Smite
 [/code]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][icon name=ability_priest_atonement color=priest inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] Discipline Priest Major Cooldown Usage[/h2]



[tabs name="cds"]

[tab name="Uppies" icon=ability_priest_ascendance]

Ultimate Penitence or "Uppies" has a couple very important interactions that you should know about to maximize its value

[ul]

[li]As you cast Uppies you can "spell queue" another ability to cast as your character is flying into the air. If you spam a button like Void Shield as your cast of Uppies is finishing it will cast the Void Shield as your character is rising into the air to begin raining down Penance bolts. Timing it before your Uppies cast completes is important because if you cast it after the Uppies cast completes then it can interrupt Uppies.[/li]
[li]Uppies can also be interrupted by spell casting which can allow you to cast a spell like Smite as you are falling to the ground, in most situations this season you will want to simply channel a Penance as you fall back down to the earth but certain seasons it can be valuable to interrupt.[/li]
[li]When playing as Voidweaver you have multiple passives which increase your Atonement healing when your Voidweaver Rift is out. As a result you'll always want to cast your [b]Mind Blast[/b] to deploy your Rift, into [b]Uppies[/b], into [b]spell-queued Void Shield[/b] to maximize your output.[/li]



[/ul]
[/tab]


[tab name="Advanced Atonement Notes" icon=ability_priest_atonement]

There are many small intricacies to [spell=81749] interactions that can be confusing. Here is a quick list of interactions that demonstrate how [spell=81749] functions.

[ul]
[li]Damaging trinkets and "non-Priest" damage does not convert into [spell=81749] healing.[/li]
[li]AoE abilities like [spell=373427] and [spell=132157] only convert into [spell=81749] on one enemy struck.[/li]
[li]Reduced or increased damage taken modifiers from outside the Priest do not affect [spell=81749] healing. If the boss has an aura that makes them take 100% more damage, this does not affect [spell=81749], if the boss takes 99% less damage, that also does not affect [spell=81749], if the boss is [b]IMMUNE[/b] then you will produce [b]ZERO[/b] [spell=81749] healing.[/li]

[/ul]

[/tab]
[tab name="Timing Ramps" icon=spell_holy_borrowedtime]





One of the most challenging concepts for Discipline Priests is timing [b]when[/b] to begin your [spell=81749] application. There are two main ways to learn, and most of the time you'll have to do some trial and error to get it just right. 

With a great deal of encounters, you can focus on your Boss Mod of choice to track when an ability hits. With each encounter it can be a bit different, while you may want to ramp for the "Omega Buster" mechanic on the boss mod, that timer may track when the boss begins to cast the ability, not when the damage occurs. So, when first jumping into an encounter, you might end up ramping too early and lose some [spell=81749]s when the boss' cast actually completes. Using a notepad tool on another monitor, using Method Raid Tools or a similar Note addon in game can also help so that you can notate that this "Omega Buster" mechanic has a 5 second cast before it goes out so you'll begin your ramp around 1-2 seconds on the boss mod timer since it'll take around 6 seconds to complete your [spell=81749] application before you can begin damaging to heal. Once you get that first ramp down, you'll generally be able to ramp on cooldown [i]or[/i] at the same points on the boss mod timer as before. You can also emphasize and deemphasize boss mechanics to reduce bloat and help you properly visualize when boss mechanics are going to occur to allow you to be more focused.

"[b]Landmark[/b]" timing is a method I like to use when raid damage is activated by your raid group. Examples of this would be fights like BNexus King Salhaadar, who spawns Orbs that when killed will deal heavy raid damage. There [i]are[/i] boss mod timers for these mechanics but your raid is responsible for killing them and damage can always vary. As a result, I like to use "Landmarks" in the encounter to help me time when I will be ramping. Setting notes so you can track your progress, being aware that you will need to use some trial and error to perfect this will be extremely important. 
[/tab]

[/tabs]
